result:
Credit notes now carry the legal entity of the invoice they credit, and the full test suite passes (486 tests).

- **Entity and numbering:** A credit note takes its entity from the credited invoice. This holds even if the tenant has since moved entity. Numbers are `CN-<ENTITY>-<TENANT>-<YYYY>-<seq>`, for example `CN-MBDE-NWD-2027-00001`. Each entity, tenant and year has its own gapless sequence, kept separate from the invoice sequence.
- **Output:** `CreditNote` has a new `entity` field. It's saved only when set, and the credit CLI's text output now shows it.
- **Old data:** Old-format notes without an entity still load, and keep their old numbers. If a credit sequence file in the old layout exists, it moves under MBDE the first time a credit note is issued. Numbering then continues from the old counter. This matches how the invoice sequences were migrated in #57. `data/credit_sequences.json` doesn't exist in this repo, so nothing was migrated here.
- **Tests:** I changed three existing credit tests to expect the new number format. I added tests for a separate sequence per entity and for the old-layout migration and loading.

I closed #58 in clarity with a note on the above. I didn't commit anything.

The first `clarity-ctl start` call, made with a name and `--repo meterbill`, didn't create an epoch because no repos are registered. I started #58 by id with `--repo none` instead, so the epoch has no branch attached.
